messages:
alex: kicked off a run to decouple prefill vs decode batching. hypothesis: prefill batches are monopolizing the batch window and forcing decode into tiny, inefficient batches.
maria: ok cool — any quick numbers?
alex: quick profile dump from the canary VM:
```
prefill.avg_batch=17.9
decode.avg_batch=3.2
prefill.kernel=matmul_f16
decode.kernel=matmul_int8_small
kernel.switches/sec=24
kv_cache.hit_rate=0.72 -> dips to 0.55 during prefill storms
```
alex: decode p95 spikes to ~420ms when prefill queue fills; overall throughput dropped ~8% on rtx-a100-32g config in that run.
devon: can we reserve some budget for decode? a priority lane so prefill doesn't completely starve it.
jiwon: i tried a tiny config tweak locally: prefer_decode=true, decode_token_budget=32, prefill_token_budget=96, max_wait_ms=12
jiwon: short-run results: decode p95 down ~35%, p50 ~same, overall throughput -1.2% (looks acceptable). kv_cache.hit_rate rose ~+4%.
samir: did forcing decode priority change kernel selection behavior? we saw kernel-switch overhead before.
alex: yes — runtime was switching kernels between phases which costs ~0.6-0.9ms per request on our path. forcing decode to take f16 path (even for small batches) eliminated cross-phase switch and improved latency for decode bursts.
maria: so there's a tradeoff: decode per-token compute slightly worse but end-to-end latency better due to fewer context switches?
alex: exactly. single-token decode microcost up ~0.7ms, but batch latencies and tail improved. overall user-facing latency wins.
jiwon: one concerning reg: for long-context tests (>8k tokens) prefill batching heuristics triggered more frequent KV-cache drains/evictions. saw kv.evictions/sec spike and subsequent rare memory thrash. suspect drain timing tied to batch window alignment.
devon: proposal: phase-aware KV drain backoff — avoid aggressive eviction while decode backlog > X or decode_token_budget in use.
alex: I'm drafting a PR that introduces:
```
queue.policy = 'phase-aware'
queue.decode_priority = true
queue.token_budgets = {prefill:96, decode:32}
queue.max_wait_ms = 12
kv.drain_backoff_ms = 200
kernel.override[decode] = 'f16_matmul'
```
alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1123 (WIP, unit tests added).
maria: can we A/B this on dedicated-beta pool tomorrow? :thumbsup: we should watch p95/p99, kernel-switch counter, and kv-evict-rate.
samir: scheduled canary for pool:dedicated-beta tomorrow 10:00 UTC. i'll also add alerts for kv.evictions/sec > 5 and kernel.switches/sec > 10.
sre-bot: deploy scheduled to pool:dedicated-beta at 2024-11-14T10:00:00Z by @samir
alex: thanks — follow-up plan: after canary run, collect: p50/p95/p99 for decode and prefill, avg batch sizes, kernel switch rate, kv hit/evict stats.
jiwon: added lightweight dashboards: kernel-switch, kv-evict-rate, decode.avg_batch, prefill.avg_batch.
maria: if canary metrics look good, merge and roll to prod waves with a small ramp.
samir: i'll run the canary and post logs here. tagging @alex @jiwon for post-mortem.
alex: sounds good. next steps: tune decode_token_budget downward if small models show regression, and if long-context prefill still causes evictions we try bumping kv.drain_backoff_ms to 400ms.
maria: cool — keep notes in the PR. thanks all :eyes:
